newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm, long rally unlikely - traders.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm, long rally unlikely - traders.

text.p: Russian shares extended early gains on Wednesday after news that President Boris Yeltsin had good chances of full recovery from planned heart surgery, but traders said the market was not headed into a sustained rally.
The RTS 24-share index edged up 1.62 percent to 159.70 on $25.7 million volume after a 6 percent fall on Tuesday.
Mosenergo closed on the Russian Trading System at $0.850 after $0.832 at Tuesday's close. LUKoil traded up to $8.95 from $8.62, and Rostelekom firmed to $2.33 from $2.23.
"It is a dead cat bounce," said one trader, adding that firming prices did not mean the market was alive again. "There won't be any sustained rally from this."

"The market won't return to pre-election levels," said Alfa-Capital researcher Kristen Burton Steiner. "That pre-election rally was on good expectations. But people are not trading on good expectations with Yeltsin's health."
Analysts said uncertainty would still pressure the market until Yeltsin was clearly in control again.
U.S. cardiologist Michael DeBakey, after consultations with Yeltsin, told a news conference Yeltsin could fully recover from bypass surgery six to eight weeks after his operation.
Doctors said Yeltsin's operation would probably be held off for six to eight weeks in order to give Yeltsin a close to 100 percent chance of surviving surgery.

Burton Steiner said new investors, upon whom the market has waited for months in expectations of a new rally, were likely to put off investment to the spring, given Russian macro-economic problems such as tax arrears and the budget defitcit.
Traders said on Friday foreigners and domestic buyers supported the afternoon rally which began after positive news on Yeltsin's prospects surfaced about 1220 GMT.
"As usual, the rise began with Russian brokers anticipating Western orders," said Anton Kudryashov of Renaissance Capital.

Shares of Lenenergo, where workers are threatening to strike, rose to $0.385 from $0.356. Gazprom, which announced a 25-year, 250 billion cubic metre natural gas contract with Poland, saw shares edge up to $0.335 from $0.320.
Irkutskenergo, which announced it had applied to the U.S. authorities to make a level-one American Depositary Receipts issue, rose to $0.102 from $0.095.
Tatneft remained unchanged at $27.75 after announcing it would issue new equity through ADRs.
